finding.title: Correct the analyzer lint-rule count in docs/coding-standards.md (claims 83, actual 79)

evidence.quote: a deliberately hand-rolled explicit list (83 rules in `analysis_options.yaml`)...

finding.why: analysis_options.yaml's linter.rules block has exactly 79 entries (lines 21-99), not 83. development-guide.md's independent '~80 lints' hedge happens to be accurate; coding-standards.md's precise '83' is not, and this is the doc explicitly positioned as authoritative for the lint baseline.
finding.recommendation: Change '83 rules' to '79 rules' at coding-standards.md:695, or make the count self-verifying by having Rule 0 tooling count the block.
acceptance_criteria: docs/coding-standards.md's stated linter.rules count matches `awk '/^linter:/,0' analysis_options.yaml | grep -c '^    - '`

finding.title: Update docs/component-inventory.md and docs/api-contracts.md for the firebaseFirestoreProvider relocation to core/sync/
finding.why: component-inventory.md's 'Core Providers (lib/core/providers/)' table lists firebaseFirestoreProvider as living in lib/core/providers/, but it was moved (per DNI-333, per the provider file's own comment) to lib/core/sync/providers/firestore_instance_provider.dart. Separately, api-contracts.md claims FirestoreGatewayImpl is 'the only lib/ file allowed to import cloud_firestore', but firestore_instance_provider.dart also imports it (both are within core/sync/, so Rule 3 itself is not violated — the 'only' claim is just false).
finding.recommendation: Move firebaseFirestoreProvider's table row to a core/sync/ providers section in component-inventory.md; soften api-contracts.md's 'the only file' wording to name both sanctioned import sites.
acceptance_criteria: component-inventory.md's Core Providers table locates firebaseFirestoreProvider at core/sync/providers/firestore_instance_provider.dart
api-contracts.md no longer claims a single exclusive cloud_firestore import site

finding.title: Refresh stale audit-check/ARB-key/test-file counts in docs/development-guide.md

evidence.quote: app_en.arb, app_he.arb (~468 keys, keep in parity — see make arb-parity)
Firebase confined — firebase_auth/cloud_firestore/firebase_storage only in core/sync/ + features/auth/
echo "22/22 — Every lib/core/labels/ file touching displayNameEn/He must be variant-aware..."

finding.why: learning_tracker/Makefile's audit target runs 22 checks (not 13); lib/l10n/app_en.arb has 1421 translatable keys (not ~468 — a 3x undercount); learning_tracker/test/ has 770 *_test.dart files (not 359 — more than double). The Firebase-confinement summary also omits core/auth/, which legitimately imports firebase_auth (auth_gateway_user.dart, firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart, etc.) alongside core/sync/ and features/auth/. This file is explicitly positioned (via CONTRIBUTING.md) as 'the authoritative reference for setup, testing, and conventions' — a contributor sizing the test suite or the audit gate off these numbers gets roughly 2-3x wrong figures.
finding.recommendation: Re-derive all four figures from the live repo (Makefile check count, arb key count via the arb-parity tool, test file count, and the core/auth/ Firebase-confinement location) and update development-guide.md.
acceptance_criteria: development-guide.md's stated audit check count matches the number of numbered checks in learning_tracker/Makefile's audit target
development-guide.md's ARB key count matches app_en.arb's non-metadata key count
development-guide.md's test file count matches `find learning_tracker/test -name '*_test.dart' | wc -l`

finding.title: Reconcile contradictory ci.yml job counts in docs/architecture.md (4) and docs/deployment-guide.md (8) — actual is 7

evidence.quote: The GitHub Actions CI (`ci.yml`) runs 4 jobs on every PR and push...
Triggers: PRs to main/dev, pushes to main/dev/dev/**. 8 mostly-parallel jobs:

finding.why: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines exactly 7 top-level jobs (format-check, analyze, audit, lint, test, firestore-rules, arb-parity — confirmed by grepping the job keys at lines 15,49,102,146,185,294,359). architecture.md's CI Matrix table lists only 4 (format, analyze, test, firestore-rules), silently dropping audit/lint/arb-parity and even misnaming 'format' vs the real 'format-check' key. deployment-guide.md lists 8, double-counting 'coverage-floor' as job #6 separate from 'test' (job #5) when coverage-floor is actually a step inside the single test job. Two canonical docs disagree with each other and with the code on a fact a contributor would use to reason about what gates a merge.
finding.recommendation: Regenerate both CI sections from ci.yml's actual job list (7: format-check, analyze, audit, lint, test [incl. coverage-floor step], firestore-rules, arb-parity).
acceptance_criteria: architecture.md's CI Matrix and deployment-guide.md's job list both enumerate exactly the 7 job keys defined in .github/workflows/ci.yml

finding.title: Mark hebrew-terms.md §11 item 5 as fixed — the make audit grep already targets the right symbol

evidence.quote: The `make audit` layering grep targets a symbol name (`hebrewTermsScriptProvider`) that does not exist...
echo "7/15 — No useHebrewTermsProvider read outside core/labels..."; \

finding.why: learning_tracker/Makefile check 7 already greps for `useHebrewTermsProvider` (the real provider name), not `hebrewTermsScriptProvider` — which has zero occurrences anywhere in the repo. Every sibling item in this same numbered list (3, 4, 6, 7, 8) that got fixed carries a '— FIXED (A4)' annotation; item 5 is missing one, so the doc still presents a working control as broken. A reader could waste time re-"fixing" a grep that already works, or distrust a control that is functioning.
finding.recommendation: Add '— FIXED' to hebrew-terms.md §11 item 5, or remove it if the underlying grep-correction was folded into an earlier commit.
acceptance_criteria: hebrew-terms.md §11 item 5 either is removed or carries a FIXED annotation consistent with its siblings
